svg.text: Chromium: Vulkan Encode First, Decode Next
Decode is already HW-accelerated today through the VA-API bridge — so the first Vulkan-native backend is the ENCODER (upstream pushes begin end of July 2026); the decoder follows.
DELIVERED
Track 1 — VA-API decode port for NVIDIA (the temporary bridge)
Chromium's existing VA-API backend already served Intel and AMD GPUs with their codecs — NVIDIA was the gap. NVIDIA
delivered a VA-API port to fill it temporarily: users get HW-accelerated decode today, with zero new API plumbing.
A bridge to the future Vulkan Video work: decode is accelerated now; Vulkan replaces it underneath, for every vendor.
UPSTREAMING
Track 2 — Vulkan Video encoder FIRST (the strategic decision)
Encode is where the gap is TODAY (no HW encode path in stock Linux Chromium at all), so it goes first. Built on the Vulkan Video
Samples library, vendored and statically linked into Chromium (the libvpx/libaom pattern) and driven through a codec-neutral
VideoEncodeAccelerator backend on the compositor's own VkDevice. Working H.264 encode with the SharedImage zero-copy input
path verified on NVIDIA HW (bit-identical to staging, PSNR-gated); lights up WebRTC, WebCodecs, MediaRecorder, and Cast.
⭢ Upstream CLs to chromium.org begin end of July 2026
NEXT
Track 3 — Vulkan Video decoder (decode is already accelerated via Track 1)
Per-codec accelerator delegates (H.264/H.265/AV1/VP9) converting Chromium's parsed headers into Vulkan Std structures;
DMA-buf export with DRM format modifiers for zero-copy VideoFrames into the compositor (gfx::NativePixmapDmaBuf).
Retires the VA-API bridge and replaces per-platform VA-API/V4L2/DXVA with one cross-vendor backend.
How the work is shared
NVIDIA — the port itself: backends, library, drivers, conformance · AMD & Intel — HW acceleration bring-up and validation on their GPUs (Mesa RADV/ANV)
Google — Chromium change reviews and browser-framework improvements (notably GPU zero-copy plumbing) · Khronos Vulkan Video Subgroup — API stewardship & CTS
